_doc: The closure ledger (campaign spec 2026-08-31-reforge-full-campaign-design.md, S1.1/S1.3/S5; contract X2). One row per in-scope subsystem and per headless catalog tool. Canonical row list: reforge/ledger/rows.ts. Validate: npx tsx ledger/check.ts. Every wave child updates its rows in its landing commit; pin bumps flip touched rows to 'stale'.

rows.title: Tool result formatters (Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, task family)
rows.note: TEN of the graph's 44 `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam` methods are excised and delegated to reforge-owned modules (Write, Glob, TaskCreate from M3-B; Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate from C4/W1), 6,568 minified chars. Every one of the ten owned MODULES is standalone-complete and registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts: it ships its own constants and pure helpers, and only typed ports cross the adapter (Read's WeakMap+clock staleness prefix and tab-separator gate, Bash's background output path and task-ack envelope/ending, TaskUpdate's two agent-team predicates). The SUBSYSTEM row nevertheless stays `spliced`, not `standalone-complete`: 34 formatters remain, so the family is not owned. Coverage is honest too — the corpus renders one of Read's six result arms, one of Grep's three and the plain stdout path of Bash's six, and never truncates a Glob result; the arms it cannot reach are graded by strangle/contracts.test.ts (135 checks). DEPENDENCY EDGES (§2.4), one per effectful-port capture that leaves this row: `tool/Read` — the Read formatter's staleness prefix is a module WeakMap keyed by the result object and populated inside the Read tool's CALL path, then rendered through a Date.now()-derived day count, so it is a side channel owned by Read's execution, not data this wave can own; `subsystem/bash-executor` — the Bash formatter's background output path reads the live outputPathBindings registry, and its task-ack envelope/ending reach the background-task machinery §1.1 files under the Bash executor; `subsystem/subagent-dispatch` — TaskUpdate's completion nudge is gated on the session's agent/team identity. Read's tab-separator capture is a feature gate, and gates are neither spliced nor excluded (§3.3), so it is a port with no edge.

rows.title: Tool-result validators (Edit's validateInput and its 19 siblings)
rows.note: Split out of §1.1's 'formatters + validators' row by C4 with measured evidence: the Edit tool's error results ("String to replace not found in file.", "File has not been read yet.", the stale-read and match-count messages) are NOT produced by `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam`. They are returned by a sibling `async validateInput`, 3,317 minified chars against the formatters' 155-1,590, carrying filesystem reads, readFileState access, `tengu_edit_tool_stale_read` telemetry and gate reads — mostly `effectful-port` captures. It needs its own scenario (a deliberately missing `old_string`) and its own gate row, so C4 scoped it out rather than smuggling it in behind a formatter wave. 20 `validateInput` methods exist in chunk-fy12d89p.js. OPEN: this row is filed under C4 because that is the child that subdivided it, and C4 does not close it — the roadmap owes it a wave assignment (campaign spec Revision Notes, 2026-09-01).

captures.name: a
captures.note: derived identifier is 'a.platform'; the footprint covers its root binding 'a' (a member read has no declaration of its own)

rows.note: W3 (C6) owns the assembly pipeline: the identity-line selector, the ambient-context tail, the block partition and its cache scoping, the wire shaping, the CLAUDE.md/system-reminder injection, and the dispatched-agent prompt — plus W0a's env block, whose far side is now reached as a port BY subagent-prompt (an edge inside this row). The row stays `spliced` rather than standalone-complete: the SECTION BUILDERS behind the preset's 27 KB block (upstream OS() and its ~45 free variables) are still upstream's, and so is the per-tool serializer Eie, which the scout measured as not a clean seam and referred to the tool-runtime wave. The static-prompt gate is pinned false by S3.3, so two of the partition's three paths are graded by strangle/prompt-parity.test.ts rather than by the corpus; attestation/coverage.md records all 38 exclusions with that oracle named. Two typed-port edges leave the row: the message constructor that stamps uuid and timestamp onto the system-reminder message (session/transcript), and the prompt-cache-control builder plus the remaining-token attachment (query loop). The env-block port is an edge INSIDE the row, which is the campaign's first. W7.5 TAKES SIX OF THE SECTION BUILDERS THIS ROW NAMED AS ITS GAP, and corrects the count it named them with: the inventory is not '~20 prose sections' but 27 dynamic section records plus a six-element static head, assembled by a five-element return array in which exactly ONE element (kKe) follows the dynamic set - not the 'two-element tail' the wave first wrote - derived from the pin as research/fixtures/prompt-sections-2.1.251.json and re-derived by the gate (research/tools/extract-prompt-sections.ts, found by shape from the section-record constructor and confirmed twice - by the boundary sentinel the block partition looks for, and by the defaultSystemPrompt property every caller binds the result to). The six rows are the STATIC HEAD: the identity/security opener, # System, # Doing tasks, # Executing actions with care, # Using your tools and # Tone and style - about 11.2 KB of the preset's prose, every one of them rendered by sysprompt-preset and every solo sabotage measured RED against it. All six anchors are PROSE occurring once over the 1,802-file set, the strongest class the doctrine has and a deliberate contrast with C6's two structural anchors; two near-misses are recorded on the rows (the # Using your tools heading occurs twice inside its own function's two arms, which selectExcision ties because it counts candidates rather than spans, and the short form of the parallel-tools sentence also occurs twice). The bullet formatter is a pure-helper with fifteen call sites, owned in a shared file with upstream's copy left live; the hooks paragraph has one caller and folds in - and the fold-in still has to be DECLARED, because the capture inventory refuses an undeclared free variable, so it rides as an owned pure-helper that is derived but neither forwarded nor called. THE REMAINING GAP IS NAMED RATHER THAN IMPLIED, and W7.5's boundary review corrected how: the 27 dynamic records are still upstream's, the FIXTURE carries their SHAPE (name expression, conditional-spread flag, thunk kind, and each producer's chunk/bytes/declKind) and the per-record TAKEABILITY TABLE lives in the README's W7.5 record, because rendering is measured from the cassette and the fixture is pin-keyed with a gate phase that fails on any diff. THREE - not four - have nothing to excise: one inline thunk (endconv_deferred_hint) and two cross-chunk producers (memory -> pKe in chunk-9e2ns8ty, subagent_steer_delegation -> Rnr in chunk-bsdtxcdc). Nine of the 27 RENDER on the m1-sysprompt-preset cassette, so the class reason 'gated behind experiments, background jobs or remote surfaces the corpus does not enter' is right only for the eighteen that do not. THREE ARE TAKEABLE NOW and are named work for a later completions pass: session_guidance (O8t, 1,447 B), context_management (G8t, 291 B) and the env_info family (ZGe 55 B / H8t 127 B) - each already rendered by an existing scenario, so each is gradeable the day it is taken. The memory section stays deferred as a port-heavy S-module, and several remaining records are single string constants, i.e. variable-declarator or primitive shapes rather than function splices. So is the per-tool serializer Eie. The row stays spliced.

rows.title: Compaction: summarization prompt, compact_boundary emit, trigger policy

captures.name: bg
captures.note: exporting module 'crypto' is not part of the graph — only the import site is covered

rows.note: W4 owns the client-side compaction surface EXCEPT its drivers. Five splices: the summarization prompt (C5x's variable-declarator spike, graded by the build-time comparison against the pinned chunk's bytes), the compact_boundary constructor (upstream H1, both triggers rendered - 'manual' by slash-compact/compact-continue, 'auto' by auto-compact-threshold), the boundary's wire shaping (rSe, zero captures), the post-compaction continuation message together with the summary rewriter it calls (Cq + d1n in one owned module: d1n is a pure helper with one caller, so a separate splice of it was measurably dead - its solo sabotage came back GREEN), and the auto-compaction trigger predicate (nKn, 10 captures). EDGES: session-storage owns the identity minting behind the boundary's uuid; the query loop owns the context accounting the trigger reads (contextTokens, charsPerToken, classifyContextLevel, effectiveWindow) AND the compaction drivers themselves. NOT owned, and why: the DRIVERS (upstream zRe, the async generator that routes a true decision through the reactive path, and Tte, the reactive driver that runs the PreCompact hooks and calls the summarizer) are query-loop-shaped and deferred to C16/W13 with the rest of the turn driver; the summarization-prompt WRAPPERS (nie/hRt) share a byte-identical five-line preamble inside one chunk, which no coLiteral can separate; and MICROCOMPACTION is a reviewed exclusion rather than a scenario debt - createContextHintController returns null unless querySource starts with 'repl_main_thread' and the headless driver sends 'sdk', so the controller is null, onRequestError short-circuits and v4n can never run. Grading it would need the synthetic response corpus plus a patched querySource, i.e. an engine-behaviour change rather than fault injection. SEGMENT COMPACTION, MEASURED BY W7.5 RATHER THAN DEFERRED: the from/up_to variant is upstream E4n (4,710 B, exported from chunk-fy12d89p) - NOT hRt, which is only that path's summarization-prompt builder and is what every earlier prose site named. E4n is the third and only five-argument caller of H1, so user_context, messages_summarized and the un-suppressed continuation arm are its alone. It has ONE caller bundle-wide: handleSummarize on the interactive session controller, which throws unless a terminal host is bound, reached through an Ink dialog that a double-Escape keypress opens. Zero control-protocol subtypes delegate to it (all 52 arms filtered), no Query method or Option reaches it, /compact lands on the three-argument call, and the PreCompact hook cannot tell it apart because E4n passes trigger:'manual'. So the three W4 exclusions it guards are SEAM-UNREACHABLE, not a coverage debt, and the variant routes to C16/W13 with zRe and Tte rather than to a completions wave. The READER side is reachable headlessly - a resumed transcript re-serializes both fields - so a later wave wanting the reader graded can seed a fixture transcript; the writer is the ceiling. Evidence: research/2026-09-02-w75-segment-compaction-reachability.md.

rows.note: W5 owns the DISPATCHERS: twenty-one entry points covering TWENTY-TWO of the twenty-four hook events the engine is measured to fire headlessly (one function serves Stop and SubagentStop; the two model-switch dispatchers are the gap named below). The twenty-first arrived in C9's boundary-fix round: VNt/PermissionDenied had been OPEN across two waves because its sole call site is guarded on a denial whose decisionReason is the auto-mode classifier's, and no prompt makes a classifier deny. What creates it is a chosen 400 on the classifier's OWN API call at record time, which reaches upstream's fail-closed arm - so the event that looked like it needed a scarier command needed a fault placed where the classifier lives. Each owns one event's hook-input record -- its field set and ORDER, which is the byte stream a command hook reads on stdin -- plus the guard that decides whether to dispatch at all and the options the executor is asked for. THREE SHAPES: fourteen are async generators that stream their executor's results into the conversation; six await a second executor (AE) because their callers have no conversation left to stream into -- and tz/PreCompact goes further, reducing its results to a verdict the compactor obeys (custom instructions, a display message, a blocking reason), which is the only place in this subsystem where hook OUTPUT is behaviour rather than a stream; and CUt/FileChanged is neither async nor a generator, reaching NEITHER executor -- it returns the watcher-hooks helper's promise for its caller to chain. Six distinct upstream pure helpers came with them as owned helpers rather than ports, captured ten times across the rows: the hook fan-out rule and its two agent-context predicates (strangle/modules/shared/hook-agent-context.js), the last-assistant-message pair (strangle/modules/shared/assistant-text.js), and the plain-object test that decides chain eligibility. The row is SPLICED, not standalone-complete, and the gap has TWO halves. (1) THE SHARED EXECUTORS: the 23 KB generator executor (upstream Qxt, reached through jy/Xxt), its awaiting sibling AE, and the watcher-hooks helper zxt that FileChanged and CwdChanged share -- hook matching, command/callback/http/mcp invocation, timeouts, cancellation -- which the W5-W7 scout measured S-MODULE-shaped and which S2.3 says is owned behind a designed port rather than transcribed. Whichever wave takes them inherits getMatchingHooks (Rzn), the agent-context result filter (Xxt) and the headless-suppression wrapper (jy) with them. (2) THE TWO MODEL-SWITCH DISPATCHERS, mdt/PreModelSwitch and gdt/PostModelSwitch, which FIRE headlessly (measured on a /model turn) and are deliberately not spliced. They are the family's only stateful members: between them they reach a plugin loader, a model prefetch and validation preamble, a per-session decision holder that gdt MUTATES (landedOn, a pending queue, an inFlight promise set) and a fire-and-forget promise the caller never awaits -- roughly seventeen forwarded ports each. S2.3 puts a stateful core behind a designed port rather than transcribing it, and doubling this subsystem's capture inventory for two events is not that design. Recorded here so the remainder is a decision rather than an omission. WHICH EVENTS FIRE, MEASURED THREE TIMES, AND THE MEASUREMENT WAS THE HARD PART. The wave's first probe drove ONE batched tool turn with CALLBACKS only and reported eight live events. C8's boundary review found that negative vacuous -- the turn created none of the missing firing conditions -- and re-measured TWELVE. C8's second round found the re-measurement still choosing its own watched list by judgment, so three live events (PostCompact, TaskCreated, Notification) sat outside the measurement entirely and six more were never asked. The population now comes from upstream's own dispatcher registry (33 events, snapshotted as research/fixtures/hook-registry-2.1.251.json and re-derived by the gate), with one named firing condition per event: TWENTY-THREE fire, none of the created conditions came back dead, and ten stay OPEN with their conditions named rather than being counted as negatives. THE MECHANISM CLAIM IS CORRECTED. The boundary round's story -- that a callback reaches a dispatcher only if that dispatcher hands the executor a session hooks registry -- is refuted by the bundle. Options.hooks entries are NOT registry entries: the initialize handler tags them origin:sdkHost and pushes them into a global store, and the lookup every executor performs (IE, chunk-fy12d89p offset 538966) returns that store's entry for the event unconditionally, merged with the settings layers. SessionStart's callback silence is a TIMING artifact -- its dispatch precedes host-hook registration -- not structural unreachability. What remains true is the byte fact underneath it: vUt, tz and EE call their executor with no registry, which is why the owned modules forward none. No claim is made about SDK-declared events outside the registry: nothing outside it can fire. Edges, all effectful ports: the working-directory reader and the base hook-input builder (session identity + app state), the child agent's transcript path (session storage), the background-task registry's wire projection and the session cron list (moat tools / subagent dispatch), and the three execution helpers. The row's title says "+ hooks chunks" and the census that named them was WRONG (W5-W7 scout S0, re-measured): chunk-7g4v1yq9 is a bundle-wide constants chunk with 521 consumers, chunk-x5kv85y3 is the remote device-hook templates and off the headless path, and chunk-scxwkz2z is a pure named-export barrel over the engine chunk with zero code of its own -- though it is not inert: the app's own shutdown() reaches SessionEnd through it by dynamic import, which is the third SessionEnd caller and the one the ordinary-teardown fire comes from. There is no hooks chunk to own; every implementation is a free function in chunk-fy12d89p.js, which is why W5 is pure S-method. W7.5 ADDS THE FAMILY'S TWENTY-SECOND ENTRY POINT: AUt/CwdChanged, FileChanged's near-twin (114 B against 115, differing in the binding, the event literal and two record fields, and reaching the same watcher-hooks helper). It was not spliceable before because nothing had ever created its firing condition - W5 left the event OPEN, correctly. The condition is one Bash 'cd' that persists past its command: the tool appends a pwd write to every command and reads it back, and a move calls the cwd-changed notifier. Measured FIRED, then recorded as hooks-cwd-change; solo sabotage reddens that scenario on the events surface with requests identical, and the faithful build is green. One gate further in decides whether the dispatcher is reached at all, and it is worth recording because it contradicts the SDK's own shape: the notifier consults the SETTINGS layer and plugin hooks only, not the global store Options.hooks callbacks land in - so a callback alone arms nothing and both the probe phase and the scenario register their matcher through Options.settings. AND W7.5 RAN THE EXECUTOR DESIGN PASS (research/2026-09-02-w75-hook-executor-design.md), which changed the size of the gap and corrected three of the names this row used. THE LAYER IS ~56 KB, NOT ~30: Qxt 23,385 B and AE 6,323 B, plus two functions no prior scoping named at all - Nq (7,209 B, the command-hook subprocess runner, called by BOTH executors AND by three non-hook callers) and Fq (5,993 B, the JSON-contract interpreter, called only by Qxt) - plus Rzn 3,129, Xxt 964, Wie 398, jy 261, zxt 298 and a ~13.9 KB belt of already-pure helpers. THREE NAME CORRECTIONS, each of which changes a decision. (1) getMatchingHooks is TWO functions: Rzn matches, and Wie resolves the SOURCES; owning Rzn alone owns no sources. (2) The session hooks store is not IE - IE is a composed layer reader; the store is class k2e, and its fields are PUBLIC, which is why this is the right first S-module where W10's Bash executor is blocked on private fields. (3) jy suppresses on SHUTDOWN, not on headlessness: its predicate is one process-wide committed flag set only in exit paths, and on shutdown six events hang forever while the rest return silently. THE ARCHITECTURE DECISION: AE is NOT Qxt's wrapper and must not share one core with it - their return types are disjoint, AE never calls Fq and silently drops the whole hookSpecificOutput permission contract, two of its arms are stubs, and its ordering is index order against Qxt's completion order; a unified core would make AE honour fields upstream drops on thirteen events. Nine ports proposed (source, scheduling, process, transport, model, environment, event-stream, telemetry, host-effects) plus a conditional served-call port that may ship as a throwing stub; behind those cuts about 27 KB is pure or pure-once-ported and the effectful residue to write is about 12 KB. IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT A COMPLETIONS-WAVE ITEM and W7.5 does not start it: the oracle needs the interleaved-event-log rewrite BEFORE the first module (cleanup pairing for per-hook derived signals is a property only an ordered log can state), plus stdout-CHUNK reproduction (async detection fires on the first chunk containing a brace) and non-settling-path grading (the shutdown arm awaits a promise that never resolves); and the corpus needs a multi-hook scenario and a repeated-spawn-failure scenario that do not exist. Staged 0-5 in the design doc, with AE and zxt before Qxt.

rows.title: Permission decisions + rule matching/parsing
rows.note: W6 owns the decision chain from the pre-check down, the mode axis end to end, and the headless broker's return leg: TEN splices here plus C5x's deny-stamping link (whose value this wave's oracle now grades, closing the C7/C9 carve-out), and TWO owned functions in shared/ that are deliberately not rows. THE ASK-RULE PREDICATE AND THE SAFETY-CHECK FINDER WERE TWO MORE OF THE NOT-ROWS AND ARE NOW ROWS OF THEIR OWN, and the adjudication they replace is worth recording because every part of it was checkable and wrong. It said their remaining callers were the mode-aware body's GATE-DEAD auto/dontAsk arms: `auto` is not gate-dead (this same wave measured it accepted through both paths), and the dontAsk half never applies because the mode-aware body returns on dontAsk before reaching either call. It said the corpus's decisions carry NO decisionReason at all: every Bash denial carries subcommandResults, which is exactly the shape both functions recurse into. And the two callers left after the pre-check and the rule checker take their copies are on the LIVE headless Bash path - the multi-cd aggregator and the subcommand merge's tie-break - kept quiet not by a gate but by needing a command SHAPE no cell wrote. What actually hid them was the pair of twins: one returned undefined and one returned false, which is what the healthy functions return on every input the corpus produces. Inverted twins plus the corpus's first `auto` cell (perm-auto-classifier-deny) redden both. A DARKNESS VERDICT IS A MEASUREMENT, and it inherits the limits of the twin and the corpus it was taken against. The message builder (ql, 45 call sites) is different: it RUNS on every tool call and its output is absorbed before it reaches any observable a headless corpus can produce — an ask's message never travels to the SDK host, and the one path on which it reaches the model takes the rule checker's annotating arm, which keeps the tool's own message. All three are graded against upstream's bytes by the parity oracle, and two control_response envelopes recorded on subsystem/control-protocol. A FIFTH was measured DARK and dropped in the same way: Uct/classifierOnlyStreakActive runs on the allow arm of every tool call in every mode, and its answer is pinned false by the disabled streak gate, so the maximal twin — return true always — leaves both covering scenarios byte-identical; the row had been carried as live on a RED the gate inferred from a non-zero exit rather than from a graded verdict. A FOURTH function was measured off the headless path and dropped outright: K0/setPermissionModeWithGuards joins the guard to the transition and reads like the set_permission_mode seam, but the headless runtime's handler calls the guard DIRECTLY and applies the mode itself, so even a twin that refused every mode change left a mode walk green. Its two ends are both owned and both live, so only the joint is unowned. Fourteen recordings now, three of them added by C9's boundary-fix round: perm-working-dir closes the workingDir decisionReason cell, perm-auto-classifier-deny closes the classifier one (a chosen 400 on the classifier's OWN API call reaches upstream's fail-closed arm), and the re-recorded perm-mode-walk finally executes the plan-with-bypass disjunct its exclusion had described. Graded by strangle/permissions-parity.test.ts (2,508 comparisons, 49 controls) over the axes research/fixtures/permission-surface-2.1.251.json derives from the bundle: six modes, three rule behaviours, eleven decisionReason kinds. THREE NAMED GAPS, all deferrals rather than omissions. (1) `von`, the 11.6 KB mode-aware decision body ABOVE the pre-check: sixty free variables, a model-classifier call, a mutable per-session denial counter — a §2.3 designed port, not a transcription. (2) `createCanUseTool`, the broker's own class method: five mutable maps on its receiver plus thirty-five module imports, the same shape. (3) `Dd`, the chain's two-line entry point, carries no string literal at all and is not takeable by the anchor mechanism; both of its neighbours are owned. A fourth, `eln`/initializeToolPermissionContext (5.4 KB, sixty free variables, filesystem and settings I/O), belongs with the settings layer rather than with the decision chain. The row cannot close on any of them.

captures.name: ar
captures.note: exporting module 'crypto' is not part of the graph — only the import site is covered

rows.note: W6 took the two response ENVELOPES ahead of W7 (the can_use_tool round trip is the only control request the permission chain itself issues). W7 owns the REQUEST leg for the four subtypes with a named handler: initialize (the handler AND the ~1 KB payload it answers with), set_permission_mode, set_model and set_max_thinking_tokens. THE LADDER ITSELF IS NOT TAKEN, and that is a shape decision rather than a deferral: research/fixtures/control-protocol-2.1.251.json derives 52 else-if arms over 54 subtypes, seventeen of which carry a loop-control jump relative to the enclosing for-await and all of which close over the frame handler’s locals. An excised arm would have to hand loop control back through a return value, which is a different mechanism rather than a generalisation of an existing one. GAPS, named rather than implied. (1) The interrupt arm is INLINED — no named handler — and its five helpers are the auto-react and task-notification subsystems rather than this one (kill-auto-react-subscriptions plus four artifact/task-notification partitioners, four of them in chunk-fy12d89p). Their firing condition is an interrupt with live tasks, artifact subscriptions or a queued command, and the corpus’s interrupt scenario creates none of those, so the row is OPEN with that condition named and belongs with W8’s task family. Nothing here claims they are dark: no twin has been measured against a population that reaches them. (2) rewind_files (Tf, 485 B) is takeable and anchorable but has no scenario of its own; the probe FIRES the arm, and nothing grades its answer. (3) mcp_message (QKn, 58 B) is one line into the MCP transport and belongs with W11. (4) The other 48 arms are peripheral: 16 serve subtypes no installed SDK can send at all, and a dozen more reach outside the harness entirely. MEASURED: 38 of the 54 subtypes FIRE on the headless seam, none is dead, and 16 are OPEN each with a written reason (w7/probe-control-subtypes.ts).
